## TL;DR

Round 2 closes the three review findings on the Security screen. The Telegram unbind, disconnect and reassign actions now use the shared confirmation dialog, not native `confirm()`. Telegram links and the audit log show a plain-English error with a retry when they fail to load, instead of their empty states. A second Enter on Add user no longer sends a second request. The browser QA test grew from 34 to 43 cases and passes, and the test for the double submit fails when its guard is removed. The QA note now lists the native controls that remain elsewhere in the UI, so the next pass doesn't re-discover them. Those are out of scope here and need a follow-up task.

## Work and rationale

The review said the Security screen still had three native `confirm()` calls (unbind, disconnect, reassign), two silent load catches, and an unguarded Add user. I grepped the whole UI before editing. The grep confirmed the three calls in `AuthSettingsPanel.vue`, and it found more native calls in other files: `SystemResourcePanel.vue`, `TelegramSettingsPanel.vue`, `TaskDrawer.vue`, and native `<select>` in `DebugPanel.vue` and `TunnelDrawer.vue`. I fixed the ones on this screen and recorded the rest in the QA note. Fixing them in this task would widen its scope beyond the sign-in and users screens.

The Telegram fix follows the users fix from round 1. Each action has a pending-state ref and a shared `ConfirmDialog`. Reassign keeps the target the user chose when the dialog opened, so the dialog confirms what was selected, not whatever the select shows later. I checked the dialog copy against the panel's own text. I removed a claim that reassignment moves sessions and bindings, because I hadn't verified it against the server.

Telegram links and the audit log now set an error ref in their catch blocks, and the template shows the error with a Try again button before the empty state. Add user got the same in-flight guard as the sign-in forms: a repeat Enter returns early while the first add is pending.

## Approaches tried

I first wrote the double-Enter test without checking that it could fail. To confirm it catches a regression, I removed the guard, rebuilt the UI, and ran that one test. It failed with two POST requests. I restored the guard and rebuilt. Rebuilding matters: the browser test serves the built app, so a source-only mutation proves nothing. My first mutation attempt skipped the rebuild and falsely passed, and I caught that before recording any result.

## Challenges and blockers

The formatter reflowed the test file between edits, so my first attempt to edit the `Reply` type failed to match. I re-read the file and retried. Nothing else blocked the work.

RepoOS had already finalized round 1's engineering report and moved its draft out of `.repoos/engineering-report-drafts/`. This draft is a new one for round 2. I did not edit the stored round-1 report.

## Key learnings

A mutation check is only meaningful if the artefact under test is rebuilt. The browser suite exercises the built `dist`, so a source change without a rebuild tests the old code.

An empty state and an error state must come from different signals. The Telegram and audit panes both showed "No … yet." on failure because their catch blocks did nothing. Setting an explicit error ref in the catch fixes the whole class, and the test asserts the empty copy is absent.

Keep the QA note's "not fixed" list grounded in a grep, not in a reviewer's list. Two files the review named had no native calls when I searched, so I left them off.
